headline: Wall Street snaps a three-day losing streak as a pause in soaring bond yields triggers a moderate market bounce. U.S. stocks rebounded on Wednesday as a relentless march higher in global bond yields and oil prices took a brief breather. Investors weighed a cooler-than-expected ADP private payrolls report against ongoing geopolitical concerns regarding military escalations between the U.S. and Iran, allowing large-cap tech and corporate earnings stars to reclaim some ground.

Market sentiment remained heavy following fresh U.S. military strikes against Iranian rocket launchers around the Strait of Hormuz, which prolonged energy supply concerns and intensified pro-inflationary macro risks.

headline: Wall Street slides to close out August as U.S.-Iran military skirmishes spark an oil spike. Major indices slipped on Monday after U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz. The sudden military flare-up sent crude prices surging toward $90 a barrel, re-igniting energy inflation anxieties and strengthening bets that the Federal Reserve will implement a hawkish rate hike at its September meeting.

headline: Wall Street inches lower as Chair Warsh delivers a hawkish inflation warning at Jackson Hole. Major indices pulled back on Friday as investors digested Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's debut speech. Warsh emphasized that the central bank remains fiercely committed to crushing sticky core inflation, stating that if price pressures do not steadily head toward the 2% goal, the Fed still has "more work to do". Short-term bond yields spiked, cooling down the tech-led momentum from earlier in the week.
